question: A 66-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of chest pain, palpitations, and dyspnea on exertion. He had a similar episode 3 days ago and was diagnosed with an inferior wall myocardial infarction. He was admitted and a percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty was successfully done that day. A fractional flow reserve test during the procedure showed complete resolution of the stenosis. Laboratory tests including serum glucose, lipids, and blood count were within normal limits. He was discharged the day after the procedure on a drug regimen of aspirin, simvastatin, and isosorbide dinitrate. At the time of discharge, he had no chest pain or dyspnea. Presently, his vitals are normal and ECG at rest shows new T-wave inversion. Which of the following is the most reliable test for rapidly establishing the diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "T-wave inversion on ECG at rest" -> "suggests myocardial ischemia or infarction" -> "raises suspicion for acute coronary syndrome" -> 80% CHAIN: "T-wave inversion on ECG at rest" -> "indicates myocardial injury" -> "may be a sign of ongoing ischemia" -> 75% CHAIN: "T-wave inversion on ECG at rest" -> "indicates myocardial repolarization abnormality" -> "can be a marker of cardiac pathology" -> 80%
enhanced_information: T-wave inversion on ECG at rest in this patient suggests myocardial ischemia or infarction, raising suspicion for acute coronary syndrome. The most reliable test for rapidly establishing the diagnosis in this case is cardiac troponin T, as it is a highly specific marker for myocardial injury and is commonly used in the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome.
analysis: The core medical principle in this case is to rapidly establish the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome in a patient presenting with chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, and new T-wave inversion on ECG. Given the enhanced information provided, T-wave inversion suggests myocardial ischemia or infarction. Cardiac troponin T is the most reliable test for rapidly establishing the diagnosis in this scenario as it is a highly specific marker for myocardial injury and commonly used in the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome.
